stem: A clinician gives a verbal instruction, the receiver repeats the message back, and the sender confirms that it was understood correctly. Which communication technique is being used?
rationale: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS defines closed-loop communication as a three-step process in which the sender initiates a message, the receiver provides feedback confirmation, and the sender verifies that the message was received correctly. A is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize the three-step structure of closed-loop communication.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)
source_version_date: Last reviewed May 2023; current page checked 2026-08-17
source_locator: Three key elements of closed-loop communication
source_claim_supported: Closed-loop communication uses sender initiation, receiver feedback confirmation, and sender verification.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — communication and interprofessional collaboration

source_original.stem: During a code, the physician gives a verbal order for a medication, and the nurse repeats the order back before administering it, then confirms it was given. This communication pattern is known as:

options.A: Closed-loop communication confirms a message through repeat-back and sender verification
options.B: Closed-loop communication is unnecessary during emergencies because it delays treatment
options.C: Closed-loop communication is intended only for low-risk routine conversations between staff
options.D: Closed-loop communication means giving an order once without receiving any confirmation

source_original.rationale: Closed-loop communication — in which the receiver repeats back an order or instruction, and the sender confirms it was correctly received — is an evidence-based communication technique particularly valuable in high-stakes, time-critical situations like emergencies/codes, helping reduce the risk of miscommunication-related errors.
source_original.source_detail: Three-step closed loop: sender initiates, receiver confirms, sender verifies; last reviewed 2023-05; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Removed the medication-code context to avoid mixing communication recognition with verbal-order procedure; retained the exact AHRQ three-step definition.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A names the described process.
audit_findings.cueing: Concise parallel labels; no clinical-order cue.
